title: MJ-12 scientists really were involved

tellings.quote: these scientists who were supposedly in the Majestic 12 group, if that was even its real name, that's all nonsense. It's just San Freriedman made the whole thing up." That's not true. They were involved.

plain: Whitley Strieber, a guest who says he has met alien beings, tells Michels that the scientists said to belong to Majestic 12, a secret group said to have handled crashed saucers, really were involved. He rejects the claim that the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman "made the whole thing up," and mentions the scientist John von Neumann. The names come from a disputed briefing paper for president-elect Dwight Eisenhower, dated 1952, which turned up anonymously on film in 1984 and was studied by Friedman and others. It lists Vannevar Bush, Detlev Bronk, Jerome Hunsaker, Donald Menzel and Lloyd Berkner among its members, and says that "A similar analysis of the four dead occupants was arranged by Dr. Bronk." The paper is where the names come from, and it attests their part only as far as it is genuine. The step from being named in it to having done the work is Strieber's.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists five scientists, "Dr. Vannevar Bush", "Dr. Detlev Bronk", "Dr. Jerome Hunsaker", "Dr. Donald Menzel" and "Dr. Lloyd V. Berkner", among its twelve members, and gives Bush, with Twining, the analysis of the craft and Bronk that of the bodies ("A similar analysis of the four dead occupants was arranged by Dr. Bronk."). The step from named in the paper to involved in the work is Strieber's; the paper is where the names come from, and it attests their part only as far as it is genuine.
